title: im_send: proactive IM messages through the push gate
description: im_send /dac 消息发送与最终回答回传: send to an explicit existing IM group with approval; private /dac final replies use their normal result pipeline.
body:
im_send(text, group_id) proactively sends to an explicitly identified existing IM group. Always supply group_id. An IM-originated Session, conversation metadata or an earlier approval does not grant a new send. Private /dac commands invoke the user’s full local DAC Session; the command and execution stay private, and only the final answer returns through its normal result pipeline. Do not call im_send to duplicate that final reply.

Use im_send only when the user asked for a group update or a result delivered there. Every send requires the normal im_send permission (default ask), then group authorization, the per-sender/per-group 20-per-hour limit, content scrubbing and quiet-hours policy. The session agent sends as itself when a member; otherwise the runtime system-pusher identity preserves attribution. An identical retry of the same durable tool call returns its recorded outcome; a conflicting target or text is rejected.

The decision is deliver, digest or blocked. deliver records a message id; digest holds the scrubbed message for the quiet-hours digest. If an external channel is configured, its failure is reported separately and does not erase a durable IM message. A blocked or unknown result is not permission to resend. Never mass-message, contact outsiders, expose workspace secrets or bypass approval by another tool.

Use when the user explicitly asks to send an update to a named existing IM group. Before calling im_send, verify the exact group_id, the requested text and the normal permission decision; after the call, record its durable message id or digest/blocked outcome and report any separate external-channel failure. The risk boundary is that an uncertain result can already represent a delivered message: do not use a new tool call to retry it, and never treat conversation metadata, a private /dac command or an old approval as authorization for a new send.
